# PRD: TripPlanner MVP

## 0. Document Purpose

This PRD defines the requirements for TripPlanner MVP — a personal web application for its author and a small circle of friends. It is the canonical requirements reference for downstream workflows. Technical decisions (stack, JWT cookie strategy, API design rules) live in the architecture spine at `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-TripPlanner-2026-06-25/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md`. Acceptance criteria and story breakdowns live in `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/epics.md`. This document covers the _what_; those documents cover the _how_.

This document defines FR-1 through FR-25. `epics.md` expands these into a more granular 31-FR breakdown that adds specificity needed for story-level implementation — the two sets are complementary, not contradictory.

## 1. Vision

TripPlanner collapses the three-tool trip-planning loop — search, cross-reference, build itinerary — into a single personal web application. A traveler heading to an unfamiliar city should be able to discover what is worth visiting, read about each place, and lock a day-by-day itinerary, without leaving the app or copy-pasting between tabs.

The motivation is personal: the author plans trips this way today and finds the current approach fragmented. Existing all-in-one tools (Wanderlog, Sygic) solve the same problem but bring feature bloat, sign-up pressure, and premium paywalls for core functionality. TripPlanner is smaller, unmonetized, and shaped exactly for the way its author plans.

The codebase is as much of the value as the product itself: this is a working, production-quality demonstration of Spring Boot REST API design alongside a tool the author will actually use.

## 2. Target User

### 2.1 Jobs To Be Done

- Discover what is worth visiting in an unfamiliar city or country quickly, without opening multiple tabs.
- Build a day-by-day plan and assign specific attractions to specific days.
- Pause mid-plan and return later without losing or redoing research.
- Share the app with a friend so they can plan their own trip without needing a walkthrough.

### 2.2 Non-Users (v1)

- Travelers needing booking or reservation integration.
- Groups planning collaboratively in real time.
- Users expecting AI-generated or personalised recommendations.

### 2.3 Key User Journeys

**UJ-1. The author plans a weekend trip to Kyoto.**
Authenticated from a previous session. Opens the app, types "Kyoto" into the search field, and selects the city. Browses the ranked Attraction list; opens Fushimi Inari Taisha, views photos and opening hours, confirms it is worth visiting. Creates a Trip named "Kyoto May", sets dates May 10–13. Adds Fushimi Inari to Day 1. Continues adding attractions across the four days. Closes the tab.

**UJ-2. The author returns to continue planning.**
Opens the app; is still authenticated. Navigates to Trips, sees "Kyoto May" with its dates and days. Opens it. All previously saved Destinations are there. Adds two more attractions to complete the Itinerary.

## 3. Glossary

- **Attraction** — A named point of interest (museum, landmark, park, etc.) retrieved from an external Provider. Identified by `providerType` + `providerId`. Full detail is fetched from the Provider on demand; only reference fields are persisted locally.
- **Provider** — An external data source. MVP: OpenTripMap (POI discovery and enrichment) and Nominatim/OSM (geocoding). Foursquare is explicitly out of scope.
- **Trip** — A user-owned planning container with a name, start date, and end date.
- **Trip Day** — One calendar day within a Trip's date range. Created automatically when dates are set; holds an ordered list of Destinations.
- **Destination** — An Attraction saved to a specific Trip Day. Persists only `providerType`, `providerId`, `name`, and `thumbnailUrl`.
- **Itinerary** — The complete set of Trip Days and their Destinations for a given Trip.
- **Discovery Session** — The flow of searching for a location and browsing the resulting Attraction list.

## 4. Features

### 4.1 Location Search & Attraction Discovery

The search field accepts city names, country names, and attraction names. Selecting a city or country result shows a ranked Attraction list for that location. Selecting an attraction result navigates directly to its Detail view. Country results surface top attractions drawn from the country's major cities. When the Provider is unavailable a non-technical error message is shown — no crash, no internal detail exposed.

**Functional Requirements:**

#### FR-1

A user can type at least 1 character and see up to 5 autocomplete suggestions labeled by result type (city / country / attraction). Search is case-insensitive with partial-match support.

#### FR-2

Selecting a city or country result shows a paginated ranked Attraction list (max 20 per page, ranking by popularity/rating). Realizes UJ-1.

#### FR-3

Selecting an attraction result navigates directly to the Attraction Detail view for that attraction. Realizes UJ-1.

#### FR-4

When no results match the input, the UI displays "No results found".

#### FR-5

When the search Provider is unavailable or returns an error, the UI displays "Search service is temporarily unavailable" without crashing or exposing internal details. Satisfies NFR-3.

#### FR-6

Each Attraction in the list displays: name, category/tags, rating/popularity indicator, and thumbnail image. Missing fields show a placeholder.

#### FR-7

For a country search result, the Attraction list draws from the country's major cities.

---

### 4.2 Attraction Details

Selecting an Attraction opens a Detail view with all available Provider data. The "Add to Trip" action is available to authenticated users; unauthenticated users see it disabled and are prompted to log in on click. Full Attraction detail is fetched on demand — nothing beyond reference fields is pre-stored locally.

**Functional Requirements:**

#### FR-8

A user can open an Attraction Detail view from the Attraction list. The view shows: name, category, description, address, opening hours ("Opening hours not available" if missing). At least one image is shown when available; a placeholder is shown when no images exist. Realizes UJ-1.

#### FR-9

The Detail view includes an "Add to Trip" action. The action is enabled for authenticated users and disabled for unauthenticated users; clicking while unauthenticated triggers the login flow (see FR-22).

#### FR-10

When multiple photos are available, the user can navigate between them. Navigation controls appear only when more than one photo exists. When no photos exist, a placeholder is shown.

#### FR-11

Closing the Detail view returns the user to the previous Attraction list.

---

### 4.3 Trip Planning & Session Continuity

Authenticated users can create named Trips with date ranges. The app generates one Trip Day per calendar day. Users build the Itinerary by assigning Destinations to days; removals and date-range reductions require confirmation. Unauthenticated users can browse freely; protected actions redirect to login with a `redirect` URL parameter so the action completes automatically after sign-in.

**Functional Requirements:**

#### FR-12

An authenticated user can create a Trip by entering a required name. The new Trip appears in the Trip list immediately. The user is navigated to the Trip Planner after creation. Realizes UJ-1.

#### FR-13

A user can set a Trip start date and end date (start ≤ end). One Trip Day is created per calendar day in the range, displayed chronologically.

#### FR-14

Reducing the date range in a way that would delete Trip Days containing saved Destinations triggers a confirmation prompt before any deletion.

#### FR-15

A user can add an Attraction as a Destination to a specific Trip Day from both the Attraction list and the Attraction Detail view. The Destination appears under the selected day immediately. Realizes UJ-1.

#### FR-16

Only `providerType`, `providerId`, `name`, and `thumbnailUrl` are persisted locally for a Destination. No full Attraction entity is stored locally.

#### FR-17

A user can remove a Destination from a Trip Day after an explicit confirmation. Dismissing the confirmation leaves the Destination in place.

#### FR-18

Unauthenticated users can freely browse search results and Attraction Detail views without being redirected.

#### FR-19

Attempting to create a Trip or add a Destination while unauthenticated redirects to login with a `redirect` URL parameter encoding the intended destination. After successful authentication, the user is returned to that destination and the original action completes. Realizes UJ-1.

#### FR-20

A returning authenticated user sees all previously created Trips on load. Opening a Trip shows its saved Trip Days and Destinations. An empty state is shown when no Trips exist. Realizes UJ-2.

---

### 4.4 User Authentication

Authentication is email/password with mandatory email verification before login is permitted. Sessions are stateless; JWT tokens are issued as `httpOnly` cookies (no `localStorage`). Password reset is in scope for MVP.

**Functional Requirements:**

#### FR-21

Unauthenticated users can browse freely (realized in §4.3); this FR gates all write operations.

#### FR-22

A user can sign up with a unique email and a password of at least 8 characters. A verification email with a unique link is sent on sign-up. The user cannot log in until the email is verified. Expired and invalid links show a clear error.

#### FR-23

A user can log in with valid credentials. On success, JWT access and refresh tokens are issued as `httpOnly` cookies; the session persists across page refresh. Invalid credentials return a generic "Invalid email or password" error.

#### FR-24

A user can log out. Both `httpOnly` cookies (access + refresh) are cleared server-side. Protected pages become inaccessible immediately.

#### FR-25

A user can request a password reset via "Forgot password?" on the login screen. A time-limited link (1 hour) is sent by email. The confirmation message is generic regardless of whether the email is registered (enumeration prevention). Clicking a valid link allows the user to set a new password meeting the minimum requirement; the old password is invalidated immediately. Requesting a new link invalidates all previous links for that account.

## 5. Non-Goals (Explicit)

- Native mobile app — web-first only for MVP.
- Booking or reservation integration of any kind.
- AI-generated or personalised recommendations.
- Real-time collaborative or shared Trip editing.
- Offline mode.
- Public Trip profiles or social sharing.
- Route optimisation or map-based Itinerary sequencing.
- Multi-user Trip ownership.
- Foursquare API integration.

## 6. MVP Scope

### 6.1 In Scope

- City, country, and attraction search with autocomplete.
- Ranked Attraction list (paginated, max 20 per page).
- Attraction Detail view with images, address, opening hours, and map.
- Trip creation with required name and date range.
- Day-by-day Itinerary management (add and remove Destinations).
- Email/password authentication with verification, login, logout, and password reset.
- Session persistence via stateless `httpOnly` JWT cookies.
- Data sources: OpenTripMap (POI discovery) and Nominatim/OSM (geocoding).

### 6.2 Out of Scope for MVP

- Everything in §5 Non-Goals.
- UX design specification — deferred to implementation phase.
- Image placeholder visual spec (icon, color, copy) — deferred to implementation phase.

## 7. Success Metrics

**Primary**

- **SM-1:** The author uses TripPlanner to plan at least one real trip end-to-end (search → detail → itinerary). Validates FR-1 through FR-20.
- **SM-2:** At least one friend completes the core flow without guidance. Validates overall usability.

**Secondary**

- **SM-3:** All user-visible operations return within ≤500 ms for 95% of requests. Validates NFR-1.
- **SM-4:** The Spring Boot API covers all MVP endpoints with demonstrably clean controller / service / repository separation.

**Counter-metrics (do not optimise)**

- **SM-C1:** Session length or time-on-site — this product optimises for task completion speed, not engagement.

## Cross-Cutting Non-Functional Requirements

#### NFR-1: Response Time

All user-visible operations (search, Attraction Detail load, Trip save) complete within ≤500 ms for 95% of requests.

#### NFR-2: Authorization

Users can only view and modify their own Trips and Destinations. Ownership is enforced at the service layer; controller-only enforcement is explicitly insufficient.

#### NFR-3: External API Resilience

When OpenTripMap or Nominatim/OSM is unavailable or returns an error, the system displays "Search service is temporarily unavailable". No crash. No internal error detail is exposed to the client.
